intro: {{nameA}} and {{nameB}} both appear on this {{course}} page in {{cityA}}, but they are not similar law schools. This page compares recorded fees, placements and ranks from our database and official sites opened in {{year}}.

IFIM Business School vs NLSIU Bangalore is a private BBA LLB against India's top-ranked public national law university on our NIRF 2025 Law list. That difference should lead the decision, not only the year fee.

sections.heading: IFIM Business School vs NLSIU Bangalore for Integrated Law: which is better in 2026
paragraphs: Choose NLSIU Bangalore if you want a public BA LLB at the National Law School of India University, which holds a NIRF 2025 Law rank of 1 on our records, and you will apply through CLAT.
Choose IFIM Business School only if you specifically want the listed BBA LLB and have confirmed that the programme is still offered, because NLSIU is a different kind of law school.

sections.heading: Fees: what our records show, and what to watch
paragraphs: For IFIM Business School we hold ₹2 lakh as BBA LLB tuition for one year. That is a year figure, not a confirmed five-year official total, and we have not multiplied it.

For NLSIU we hold Total Fees year figures of ₹3,23,815 and ₹3,13,815 for the BA LLB. These are year amounts, not a confirmed five-year official total. Confirm the current domestic fee notice on nls.ac.in.
A lower recorded IFIM year tuition does not make it a substitute for NLSIU. Recheck both official fee pages before you budget.

sections.heading: Placements compared
paragraphs: IFIM has BBA LLB rows for 2023, at ₹7 lakh average and ₹15 lakh highest, and for 2022, at ₹6 lakh average and ₹10 lakh highest. These are historical records, not promises.
NLSIU's only BA LLB placement row here is from 2019, with ₹9 lakh average and ₹18 lakh highest. Because it is before 2020, our summary table does not treat it as a current flagship figure.
Ask NLSIU for a later official recruitment report if placements matter. Do not treat the 2019 row as the 2025 outcome.

sections.heading: Admission, ranks and eligibility
paragraphs: NLSIU is listed with CLAT, which is the usual route into its BA LLB. IFIM is listed with CAT on this page; a five-year law programme is not normally a CAT course, so confirm the current official admissions test before you apply.
NLSIU holds a NIRF 2025 Law rank of 1, and the same first rank in several earlier NIRF years on our records. IFIM has no law rank on this page.

sections.heading: Location and campus
paragraphs: Both are recorded in Bangalore, Karnataka, so the city is the same. The campuses and student communities are not interchangeable.
NLSIU is a public national law university. IFIM Business School is a private business school with a listed BBA LLB. Visit the law faculty you would actually join.

sections.heading: Verdict: who should pick which college
paragraphs: Pick NLSIU Bangalore if a top-ranked public BA LLB and the CLAT route are what you want, after you have the official fee notice.
Pick IFIM Business School only if the listed BBA LLB is still offered and that private programme fits your plan, after official confirmation.
This is not a close brand comparison. Let the university type, the NIRF Law rank and the entrance test lead, not only the year fee.

faqs.question: Is NLSIU ranked first for law in NIRF 2025?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our records list a NIRF 2025 Law rank of 1 for NLSIU, along with first ranks in several earlier NIRF years. IFIM has no law rank on this page.

faqs.question: What fees are on record for these integrated law programmes?
faqs.answer: IFIM has ₹2 lakh as BBA LLB tuition for one year. NLSIU has BA LLB year totals of ₹3,23,815 and ₹3,13,815. These are not confirmed five-year official totals.

faqs.question: How do placements compare?
faqs.answer: IFIM has 2023 and 2022 BBA LLB rows, including a 2023 average of ₹7 lakh and a highest of ₹15 lakh. NLSIU's only BA LLB row here is from 2019 and is too old to treat as current.

faqs.question: Which entrance exams are listed?
faqs.answer: NLSIU is listed with CLAT. IFIM is listed with CAT, which is unusual for a five-year law programme, so confirm the official admissions test before you apply.

faqs.question: Are both campuses in Bangalore?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both are recorded in Bangalore, Karnataka, though they are very different institutions.

faqs.question: Is NLSIU a government university?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our records list NLSIU as a public university and IFIM Business School as a private institute.
